listings.mrt_info: 4 min (300 m) from NE17 Punggol MRT Station

agent_evaluation.summary: Mass-market Punggol 2BR priced right at the URA median ($1645 vs $1652) with deep liquidity (215 txns) and a genuine 6.97% resale CAGR backed by the Punggol Digital District build-out. The 300m walk to Punggol MRT/interchange and 882-unit scale support a clean exit, but documented estate wear caps the upside.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: Priced at median PSF with a reliable 6.97%/yr resale appreciation (215 transactions) and best-in-class connectivity (300m to NE17 Punggol interchange + future bus/LRT hub). PDD and Punggol Coast MRT are concrete catalysts. The 882-unit size gives the deepest 2BR buyer pool in the batch. Held back from Strong Buy by documented build/maintenance decline (wall cracks, vandalism, ageing water features) typical of a large mass-market block, and a sub-$1.3M price that appeals to a value-conscious rather than premium exit buyer.
red_flags: Documented estate wear/maintenance decline (cracks, vandalism, damaged facilities) in a large 882-unit block
Mass-market profile means appreciation tied to OCR/Punggol demand cycle, not a premium location
catalysts: Punggol Digital District jobs and SIT campus driving tenant/buyer demand
300m to Punggol MRT interchange + future Punggol Coast MRT
Deep 215-transaction liquidity supports a clean 5-7yr exit
agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Solid 2BR tenant pool from PDD workers and SIT; OCR rents are modest but the unit size (775sqft) and MRT proximity keep it leasable. Some rental competition from newer Punggol launches.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: 6.97% resale-only CAGR over 215 transactions is high-confidence and PDD-driven; sustainable mid-single-digit growth expected, though already partly priced in at the median.

listings.mrt_info: 8 min (660 m) from EW10 Kallang MRT Station

Freehold tenure is the one genuine positive.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: The headline freehold tenure and below-median PSF ($1247 vs $1581) are real, but this is a thin, niche asset for an investment hold. Just 16 URA transactions (vs 100+ for peers) means the 6.23% CAGR is statistically weak and the exit market is shallow; a 78-unit development has no liquidity cushion. Lorong 7 Geylang carries persistent vice/stigma that deters family and expat tenants and caps resale to a narrow value-buyer segment. The 1066sqft 2BR is oversized for the bracket, raising quantum without a premium-buyer to absorb it.
red_flags: Only 16 URA transactions — thin liquidity and low-confidence appreciation data
78-unit boutique development with no liquidity cushion
Geylang red-light-district adjacency (vice, crime, late-night disturbance) is a persistent stigma that narrows the buyer/tenant pool
catalysts: Freehold tenure (no lease decay) in an RCR-adjacent district
Paya Lebar Central / airbase-relocation transformation could lift D14 over the long run
agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Yield optically high (~5%) on cheap PSF, but tenant quality and demand are constrained by the Geylang location; expect transient/lower-end tenancy rather than stable expat demand.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: 6.23% CAGR rests on only 16 transactions — treat as indicative, not reliable. Freehold limits downside but the location stigma caps premium re-rating.

Location is the differentiator: 270m to DT30 Bedok Reservoir, reservoir/park frontage, and proximity to the Bayshore precinct + Thomson-East Coast Line build-out in Upper East Coast. Reviews confirm it is the best-kept of the Waterfront developments. The earlier Neutral call looks conservative given the current sub-median price and concrete D16 catalysts; minor humidity/mould and rush-hour traffic noise are manageable and stack-dependent.

listings.mrt_info: 21 min (1.74 km) from DT34 Upper Changi MRT Station

agent_evaluation.summary: Well-built, well-managed CDL development (648 units) at a low $1124 PSF, below median, with a strong 7.36% CAGR over 131 transactions. The fatal flaw for an investment hold is connectivity: 1.74km from Upper Changi MRT (shuttle-bus dependent), which caps tenant demand and resale to a car-owning niche. A solid home, a middling investment.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: Genuine strengths — CDL build quality, proactive management, deep 648-unit liquidity, below-median PSF ($1124 vs $1206), and 7.36% CAGR over a healthy 131 transactions. But location is the binding constraint: at 1.74km/21min to the nearest MRT it relies on a shuttle bus, which structurally limits the tenant pool (transit-dependent renters skip it) and resale appeal. At 21 years old (~78yr lease remaining) lease decay is starting to matter. The appreciation rate likely reflects a low base off the 2005 vintage rather than a durable forward catalyst.
red_flags: 1.74km from MRT (21min walk), shuttle-bus dependent — caps tenant and resale demand
21-year-old leasehold (~78yr remaining); lease decay becoming material
catalysts: CDL build quality and strong management reputation supports value retention
Below-median PSF with deep 648-unit liquidity
Tampines/Pasir Ris regional growth (CRL, Tampines Regional Centre) as a broad area tailwind
agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Below-average for an investment 2BR: poor MRT access deters the transit-reliant tenant majority; demand skews to car-owning families, a smaller pool. Spacious layout is a partial offset.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: 7.32% CAGR is reliable (131 txns) but likely off a low 2005-vintage base; forward appreciation constrained by lease decay and weak connectivity.

listings.mrt_info: 15 min (1.2 km) from SE4 Kangkar LRT Station

The 5.41% CAGR is the weakest in the batch, confirming muted demand. Resort-style landscaping is a livability plus, not an investment thesis.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: Affordable $1.0M quantum and a sub-median PSF make it look cheap, but cheapness here reflects a connectivity penalty rather than value. The nearest rail is Kangkar LRT 1.2km away — no MRT within walking distance, which structurally suppresses both tenant demand and the resale buyer pool. At 5.41%, its resale CAGR is the lowest of all ten condos despite 139 transactions, signalling genuinely softer appreciation rather than a data artefact. Build quality and quiet, well-landscaped environment are real but are own-stay merits. For a 5-7yr investment hold the exit liquidity and growth case are simply weaker than the better-connected peers.

listings.mrt_info: 5 min (440 m) from EW9 Aljunied MRT Station

The 1996 lease leaves only ~70 years, no MRT is within walking distance, and the 60-transaction sample is the thinnest of the batch. A speculative en-bloc punt, not a clean investment.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: The 8.61% CAGR is the highest in the batch but is the least trustworthy: it sits on only 60 transactions in an ageing (1996 lease, ~70yr remaining) estate where pricing is buoyed by en-bloc hope rather than fundamentals — and there is currently no en-bloc on the table. Lease decay is now material: under-75-year leases face CPF/financing restrictions that shrink the buyer pool over a 5-7yr hold. The blank MRT field confirms no rail within comfortable walking distance. The low PSF reflects these defects, not a bargain. Could re-rate sharply on a collective-sale catalyst, but absent that the downside from accelerating lease decay is real — hence a balanced Neutral.

agent_evaluation.summary: Sim Lian D18 development (696 units) at a low $1399 PSF, ~7% below the $1502 median, with a 7.36% CAGR over a deep 178 transactions and a low $1.1M quantum. The persistent drawback is connectivity — no MRT within walking distance and a busy 4-lane road outside — which keeps it a balanced Neutral despite genuine value on price.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: Real positives: below-median PSF ($1399 vs $1502), the deepest data confidence in the batch (178 txns, 7.36% CAGR), large 696-unit liquidity, and a low $1.1M quantum that widens the buyer pool. But the blank MRT field and a busy 4-lane arterial road outside are structural negatives for an investment hold — the transit-reliant tenant majority is deflected and resale appeal is capped. Design gripes (units facing each other, no direct reservoir access despite the name) further dull the premium-buyer case. Value on price, but the connectivity gap balances it to Neutral.
